title: Area = ½ab sin C
examples: When do I use this formula instead of base times height?
If I know the area and two sides, can I find the angle?
Does the order of the sides matter in this formula?

explain.say: Today we learn a way to find triangle area. This formula uses sine of an included angle. It is very useful for certain triangles.

items: Area formula: Area = ½ab sin C

explain.say: This formula needs two sides and the angle between them. The angle must be included between those two sides. Think of it as a sandwich.
Let us look at an example. Suppose sides a and b are five and eight. The angle C between them is sixty degrees. The area is half times five times eight times sine of sixty degrees.

Calculating this gives us the area. The area is twenty times the sine of sixty degrees. Since sine of sixty degrees is the square root of three divided by two, the area is twenty times the square root of three divided by two. This simplifies to ten times the square root of three.

Now we try a reverse problem. Suppose the area is twenty-four. The two sides are six and ten. We need to find the angle C. We set up the equation twenty-four equals half times six times ten times sine of C. This simplifies to twenty-four equals thirty times sine of C.

faq.q: What does 'included angle' mean in this formula?
faq.a: It means the angle that is trapped or squeezed between the two sides you know. You must use the angle between the sides a and b.
asks: Which angle goes with which sides?
What is the angle between the sides?

faq.q: Can I use this if the angle is obtuse, like one hundred degrees?
faq.a: Yes, you can use it for obtuse angles. You just need to make sure your calculator is set to degrees mode. The formula works fine.
asks: Does the angle have to be sharp?
What if the angle is bigger than ninety degrees?

faq.q: If I know the area and two sides, how do I find the angle?
faq.a: You rearrange the formula to find sine of C. Then you use the inverse sine function on your calculator. This gives you the angle C.
asks: How do I solve for the angle?
What is the inverse sine function?

faq.q: Is this formula only for right-angled triangles?
faq.a: No, this formula is specifically for non-right-angled triangles. It is more general than basic trigonometry rules.
asks: Is this better than using base times height?

faq.q: If I use radians instead of degrees, what changes?
faq.a: You must use radians for all your angle measurements. The formula structure remains the same, but the calculator setting must change.
asks: Degrees or radians for this formula?
How do I switch my calculator mode?

facts: The formula requires two known sides and the angle between them.
The sine function must be calculated for the included angle.
If you find sine of C, you must use the inverse sine function to find C.
The result of this formula gives the area in square units.

quiz.say: A triangle has sides of seven and nine. The angle between them is forty degrees. What is the area?
quiz.why: You correctly multiplied half times seven times nine, and then multiplied that by the sine of forty degrees.

wrong.0: You forgot to multiply by half, making the area too large.
wrong.1: You added the sides and the angle instead of using the sine function.
wrong.2: You used the wrong angle; the angle must be the one included between the two sides.

quiz.say: If the area is thirty and the sides are six and ten, what is the angle between them?
quiz.why: You correctly isolated sine of C by dividing the area by half times six times ten.

wrong.0: You only divided the area by one of the sides, ignoring the other side.
wrong.1: You forgot to multiply by half, making the sine value too small.
wrong.2: You added the sides together before dividing, which is incorrect for the formula.

quiz.say: A triangle has sides of twelve and twelve. If the area is sixty, what is the angle between them?
quiz.why: You correctly set up the equation by dividing the area by half times twelve times twelve.

wrong.0: You incorrectly used the semi-perimeter instead of the product of the sides.
wrong.2: You forgot to multiply by half, making the sine value too small.
wrong.3: You added the sides together instead of multiplying them.
